$comment: SLOP-3: starting a BLOCKED issue asks Cancel / Start anyway / Stacked PR, byte-identical x4 (web lib/blocked-start.ts, desktop domain blocked_start.rs, iOS BlockedStart.swift, Android BlockedStart.kt). A stacked start builds the whole dependency LINE bottom-up and is PROMPT TEXT only (the playbook's follow-up rule carries it from run to run): no stack plan on the server, no relay frame. Two pure steps. (1) stackLine(subjectId, relations, issues): walk DOWN from the subject over open direct blockers (openBlockers): none = stop; exactly one = it joins the line and the walk continues from it; more than one = fork (the issue that has them); an issue seen twice = cycle. Result: line (the issues BELOW the subject, BOTTOM FIRST), fork, cycle. (2) stackPlan({pickedCount, subject, line, fork, cycle}): the first matching reason in the order of `reasons` disables the button with its note; else base = the line member NEAREST the subject with prState 'open' and a non-empty branch (null when none), run = the line members ABOVE the base bottom-first, then the subject. `repo` names the first line member (bottom-first) whose repositoryId is null or differs from the subject's (a null subject repository names the bottom member). `long` when run has more than maxRun issues. `running` names the first run member below the subject that has a LIVE run. The client starts run[0] (NOT necessarily the picked issue) with stackedStartPrompt(plan, typedText): the parts below joined by a blank line: baseTemplate when base is set; lineTemplate when run has 2+ issues ({line} = run joined as '#A, then #B', {next} = run[1]); the trimmed typed text when not empty, raw for a run of one, else wrapped in textTemplate ({subject} = the last of run). planNote (shown under the graph while the button is enabled and run has 2+ issues) = planNoteTemplate with {first} = run[0], {rest} = the others joined by ', then '.

baseTemplate: Stacked on #{ident}. Before any edit: `git fetch origin {branch}`; if this branch has no commits of its own, `git reset --hard origin/{branch}`, else `git rebase origin/{branch}`. Open your PR with `exponential_pr_open({issueId, base: "{branch}"})`.
lineTemplate: This is the bottom of a stacked line: {line}. After your PR is open and your branch is pushed, start #{next} as a follow-up run on your branch (playbook: Follow-ups and follow-up runs), even under `no follow-up runs`. If more issues follow it, give it this paragraph with your own issue dropped from the line. Do not wait for it.
